newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wall St about-turn weighs on German share market.
newsitem.headline: Wall St about-turn weighs on German share market.

text.p: Wall Street's surprising overnight about-turn after an early surge weighed on German shares Wednesday morning, as the market resumed its waiting game for fresh clues on the U.S. economy.

The 30-share DAX index, playing catch-up from a surge in late electronic dealings Tuesday, opened 15.52 points higher at 3,004.47 compared to its mid-afternoon close, but was down some 24 points from Tuesday's closing level on the IBIS DAX, which also tracks post-bourse dealings.
March DTB DAX futures were down 27 points at 3,016.

"It was definitely a shock to see the Dow Jones ending lower after being up 100 points," said one dealer of Wall Street's reverse after initially surging on the back of a lower-than-expected fourth quarter labour cost report.

"People are now pretty sceptical again and they're looking out for the durable goods report this afternoon," said another dealer, noting that the range of forecasts for this key U.S. economic report due at 1330 GMT were extremely wide.
The dollar held above 1.65 marks, helping support chemical shares, which were overlooked in a recent switch to exporters.
BASF AG was trading heavily and was up 1.05 marks at 60.15 marks while Bayer AG rose 60 pfennigs to 62.20 marks.
Commerzbank AG extended its decline after Tuesday's below-forecast earnings report for 1996 to trade down 50 pfennigs at 41.90 marks.
